walkthrough_label: STACKED CASE S1-B - anticoagulated AF with iron-deficiency anaemia and an anticoagulant taken this morning
reason_answer: To have my gallbladder taken out.

presentation.summary: Mr George Mensah, 69, is booked for keyhole gallbladder removal. Known atrial fibrillation on apixaban, which the plan said to stop two days before. He is calm, well-looking and slightly pale; Hb 104, MCV 74, ferritin 9.

history.answer: Pain under the right ribs after meals, and I have been so tired for three months.
My stools have been darker for some weeks. No chest pain, no breathlessness at rest.
Atrial fibrillation, high blood pressure, chronic kidney disease (stage G3a).
Apixaban, bisoprolol, amlodipine. I took my apixaban at 7 this morning - I always do.
No anaesthetic problems in the family.

observations.note: Irregularly irregular 84: known AF, rate controlled; NEWS2 0.

examination.finding: Calm, well-looking, slightly pale, talking normally.

results.comment: Chronic kidney disease G3a (creatinine clearance about 55): matters for the apixaban timing
Known rhythm, rate controlled, not new (picture result)

scores.name: NEWS2
scores.note: Every observation in range; the rhythm is irregular

problems.label: Apixaban taken at 07:00 today although the plan was to stop it two days before
problems.why: It directly determines whether surgery can safely happen today: still active at the time of surgery, so the bleeding risk rises; a blood thinner is not reversed simply to allow elective surgery.
expected_actions: Confirm exactly when the last dose was taken
Tell the anaesthetist and the senior surgeon
Do not stop or restart on your own

problems.label: Unexplained iron-deficiency anaemia in an older man on a blood thinner (darker stools)
problems.why: It may mean gut bleeding or a cancer, which could change whether this operation is the priority at all. WHO 2024: anaemia is below 130 in men.
expected_actions: Refer for investigation of the cause (GI)

problems.label: Known atrial fibrillation, rate controlled
problems.why: It needs an anticoagulation stop and restart plan, not urgent action; confirm with an ECG that it is the known rhythm.

options.text: Request a 12-lead ECG to confirm it is the known AF

options.consequence: A new rhythm could be missed.

decisions.prompt: He is pale and his stools have been darker. What now?

options.text: Send an FBC and ferritin; tell the senior when the results are back
options.consequence: Hb 104, ferritin 9: the cause needs investigating.
A gut cancer is missed; he returns later with a bleed.

decisions.prompt: He took his apixaban at 07:00 today. What now?

options.text: Check the time and the creatinine, stop the pathway, document, and tell the anaesthetist and senior
options.consequence: The team defers: no reversal for elective surgery.

options.text: Suggest just giving a reversal agent
options.consequence: The senior declines: an unjustified reversal and a thrombosis risk.

decisions.prompt: Two independent reasons to defer. What now?

options.text: SBAR to the senior with a plan: defer, GI referral, iron and a new apixaban plan

options.consequence: The anaesthetist stops it at Sign In.

correct: SBAR to the senior and anaesthetist

incorrect.mistake: Doesn't ask when apixaban was last taken
incorrect.shows: The anaesthetist asks at Sign In; the case is stopped

incorrect.recovery: Learn: no reversal for elective surgery

incorrect.shows: Debrief; he returns later with a bleed

missed: Apixaban timing never asked: proceeds to theatre; the anaesthetist asks; the case is cancelled at Sign In
recovery: Asks belatedly, informs the anaesthetist, documents the deferral and makes the anaemia referral

debrief.independent: AF itself is stable and independent
debrief.trigger_escalation: Any anticoagulant dose inside the stop window; unexplained anaemia
debrief.if_ignored: Surgical bleeding; a missed gut cancer
debrief.remember: Ask the exact time of the last dose of every blood thinner.

asa.why: Atrial fibrillation on a blood thinner is ASA 3 in the book's list; early kidney disease and anaemia add to it.
